# ForgeFlow Pre-Existing IP Disclosure

**Legal Pack Version:** `2026-09-IR-2`

Before the Developer's first non-exempt contribution can merge, the Developer must declare one of the following states through the ForgeFlow Legal Gate.

## Option A: No relevant pre-existing IP

Use this when the Developer has no personal library, repository, framework, code, design, dataset, model, tool, template or other pre-existing material that they intend to incorporate into ForgeFlow and that could affect ForgeFlow ownership or licensing.

The Legal Gate acceptance statement is:

`I have read and accept the ForgeFlow Legal Pack v2026-09-IR-2. Pre-Existing IP: NONE.`

## Option B: Relevant pre-existing IP exists

Do **not** post confidential details, home addresses, identity documents, private repository contents or sensitive personal information in a GitHub comment.

Provide the relevant disclosure privately to Hossein Rahimi before incorporation into ForgeFlow. The private record should identify, as appropriate:

- item/project name;
- owner;
- repository or description;
- current licence or ownership status;
- intended ForgeFlow use;
- agreed ForgeFlow treatment or licence.

Then use this Legal Gate acceptance statement:

`I have read and accept the ForgeFlow Legal Pack v2026-09-IR-2. Pre-Existing IP: DISCLOSED SEPARATELY.`

For this second option, the Legal Gate remains pending until **@HoosseinRahimi** posts the version-specific approval statement generated by the workflow. This confirms only that a separate disclosure record was received/approved; the sensitive disclosure itself should remain outside the source repository.

## Continuing duty

If the Developer later wants to introduce additional pre-existing material that was not previously disclosed, the Developer must disclose and obtain approval before incorporating it into ForgeFlow.

Routine third-party dependencies remain subject to the Engineering Access & Security Policy and normal licence review.
